hints: Remember that nucleon number only counts particles in the nucleus, so focus on protons plus neutrons, not electrons.
A 2- charge means the ion has 2 more electrons than protons, so with 10 electrons the atom must have 8 protons.
Now just add those protons to the 14 neutrons given to find the total mass of the nucleus.
walkthrough:
**Recall what nucleon number means**

Think of the nucleus only. It is made of protons and neutrons, so nucleon number is their total.

$$\text{nucleon number} = \text{protons} + \text{neutrons}$$

**Work out the number of protons from the charge**

A negative ion has gained electrons. A 2- charge means 2 extra electrons compared to protons.

$$\text{protons} = \text{electrons in ion} - 2 = 10 - 2 = 8$$

**Add protons and neutrons**

Now put the two nucleus particles together to get the answer.

$$\text{nucleon number} = 8 + 14 = 22$$

options.A: 14 is just the number of neutrons. This forgets that nucleon number must include protons as well as neutrons.
options.B: The ion has 8 protons (10 electrons minus 2 for the 2- charge) and 14 neutrons, so nucleon number = 8 + 14 = 22. Well done!
options.C: 24 comes from adding the 10 electrons to the 14 neutrons (10 + 14). Electrons are outside the nucleus and are never included in nucleon number.
options.D: 26 comes from thinking a 2- ion has 2 more protons than electrons (10 + 2 = 12 protons). It is the opposite: a negative ion has more electrons than protons, so protons = 10 - 2 = 8.
